risk_if_not_implemented: Without Cross-Organization Management, unauthorized individuals, devices or services may gain access to Technology Assets, Applications, Services, Data and/or Facilities (TAASDF). Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1). No threat is rated Likely for this control; threats rated Possible include Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Authenticator Management
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to:
(1) Securely manage authenticators for users and devices; and
(2) Ensure the strength of authentication is appropriate to the classification of the data being accessed.
compensating_control_1.justification: Authenticator Management (IAC-14) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Cross-Organization Management (IAC-13.5) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Identification & Authentication for Organizational Users
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) organizational users and processes acting on behalf of organizational users.
compensating_control_2.justification: Identification & Authentication for Organizational Users (IAC-32) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Cross-Organization Management (IAC-13.5) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
